hero.headline: Knicks and Spurs open NBA Finals in San Antonio
hero.teaser: The NBA Finals tip off with Game 1 between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs.
hero.body:
The New York Knicks will face the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC in San Antonio. The Spurs earned their spot in the championship series by defeating the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory, finishing with 22 points and seven rebounds. The 22-year-old French star was named series MVP and became emotional after clinching the Finals berth. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said when explaining his reaction. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, Wembanyama's performance was supported by strong contributions from his teammates. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points, including six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper provided scoring off the bench. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, made a crucial block in the fourth quarter as the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt. After the game, Wembanyama credited his teammates' effort, saying "They don't know how much I love them, and everyone stepped up tonight."

The Thunder fought hard despite playing without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, scored 35 points and distributed nine assists but couldn't prevent his team from relinquishing their title. No other Thunder player scored more than 20 points.

Coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the tough loss but expressed confidence in his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The Spurs head into the Finals with historical momentum on their side. The last time the Knicks appeared in the NBA Finals was 1999, when they faced the Spurs and lost the series 4-1. The Knicks are attempting to win their first championship since 1973.

Julian Champagnie reflected on the Spurs' achievement after the game, noting the importance of having elite talent. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said.

League executives have weighed in on five key questions heading into the matchup. Experts have also made their predictions for which franchise will claim the Larry O'Brien Trophy and who will earn Finals MVP honors. The series features two storied franchises competing for the championship, with the Spurs holding home court advantage for the opening game.

cards.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian facility after Iran fires missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain
cards.body:
The United States military launched strikes on an Iranian facility after Iran attacked two key American allies in the Persian Gulf region. Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain, though the U.S. military reported that the Iranian weapons either malfunctioned or were intercepted by air defense systems.

Kuwait experienced significant damage to its international airport from Iranian drone strikes. The country suspended all air traffic at the facility, affecting thousands of passengers and disrupting cargo operations that are vital to the nation's commerce and travel infrastructure.

The Iranian attacks represent an escalation in regional tensions involving Tehran and U.S. partners in the Gulf. Both Kuwait and Bahrain host American military installations and serve as strategic locations for U.S. operations in the Middle East.

U.S. officials stated that defensive systems successfully neutralized threats to both nations. The American military response targeted an Iranian facility, though specific details about the location and nature of the site were not disclosed in available reports.

The incident marks a serious development in the broader conflict unfolding across the Middle East. The confrontation follows years of periodic tensions between Iran and Western powers over regional influence, nuclear programs, and Iran's support for various proxy forces throughout the region.

The exchange of strikes demonstrates the expanding scope of the conflict beyond direct combatants. The involvement of American allies in the Gulf indicates how regional disputes involving Iran and the United States increasingly affect neighboring countries and their civilian infrastructure.

Kuwait's suspension of airport operations will have far-reaching consequences for the country's economy and residents. International flights and cargo shipments form a crucial part of Kuwait's connection to global commerce, and the damage to the airport disrupts normal operations significantly.

Bahrain also faced Iranian missile fire during the same period as the attacks on Kuwait. U.S. military personnel worked to defend both nations from the incoming threats, positioning themselves as protectors of American interests in the strategically important Gulf region.

The incident underscores the volatile situation in an area critical to global energy supplies and international commerce. The Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters remain vital shipping lanes, and military escalations in the region raise broader concerns about stability and safety for international trade.

As tensions continue to rise, the potential for further military exchanges remains high. The targeting of civilian infrastructure like airports suggests that future conflicts could increasingly affect non-military targets and populations, with consequences extending beyond military personnel and installations.

The situation highlights how quickly regional conflicts can expand when multiple nations and armed groups become involved, drawing in countries across the Gulf and raising international concern about the humanitarian and economic toll of continued military action.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes as peace talks stall
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged strikes Tuesday as diplomatic efforts stalled and tensions escalated across the Middle East. Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain that were either shot down or failed to reach their targets. The U.S. military launched strikes on an Iranian facility in response to the Iranian attacks.

The confrontation spread beyond direct U.S.-Iran exchanges. Iranian drones struck Kuwait's international airport, causing significant damage and forcing a suspension of traffic. The clashes mark a notable escalation in the long-standing hostility between the two nations as peace negotiations have failed to produce results.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 10 Percent Tariffs on 60 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The US government announced plans for new tariffs of at least 10 percent on most trading partners following a forced labor investigation.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs of at least 10 percent on roughly 60 countries, citing findings from an investigation into forced labor trade practices. The levies would affect major trading partners including Canada, Mexico, and the European Union.

The administration justified the tariffs as a response to what it characterized as unreasonable trade practices that restrict US commerce. The move represents a broad expansion of US trade barriers across multiple economic sectors and regions.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Canadian officials formally asked the US and Mexico to renew the USMCA free trade agreement.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal through a letter from Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc to his North American counterparts. The agreement, which replaced NAFTA, governs commerce between Canada, the United States, and Mexico.

The renewal proposal comes amid growing trade tensions, as the Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on Canada and other trading partners. The USMCA is subject to periodic review under its terms.

cards.headline: Six states hold midterm primary elections, shaping November ballot
cards.teaser: California, Iowa, and four other states selected candidates in primary elections that will determine matchups for control of Congress.
cards.body:
Six states held primary elections to select candidates for November's midterm contests. California and Iowa voters joined four other states in choosing nominees for congressional and state races.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to a runoff election in California. In Iowa, Democrat Josh Turek secured a nomination to face Trump-backed Ashley Hinson in a bid to flip the red Senate seat.

cards.headline: Iowa sets general election matchups for governor and Senate
cards.teaser: Republican Zach Lahn and Democrat Rob Sand will compete for governor, while Democrat Josh Turek faces Republican Ashley Hinson for Senate.
cards.body:
Iowa voters have selected their nominees for competitive statewide races this November. Democrat Rob Sand, the state auditor, will face Republican businessman Zach Lahn in the gubernatorial contest. Sand ran unopposed in the Democratic primary, while Lahn won a crowded Republican primary that included U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra.

In the Senate race, Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek will challenge Republican U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson. Democrats see opportunities to compete across multiple statewide and congressional races in the traditionally Republican-leaning state.

hero.headline: Iranian Drone Attack Hits Kuwait Airport, Suspending Flights
hero.body:
An Iranian drone attack struck Kuwait International Airport, wounding several people and forcing a suspension of all flights. The Kuwaiti government reported that the airport sustained significant damage in the attack, which represents a major escalation in the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States.

The assault on Kuwait came as part of a broader series of Iranian strikes targeting neighboring countries in the Gulf region. The US military said Iran also attempted attacks on Bahrain, though those strikes were either shot down or failed to reach their targets. Kuwait, a key US ally that hosts American military personnel, has not been a direct participant in the recent hostilities.

The United States launched what it described as self-defense strikes inside Iran in response to the attacks on Kuwait and other targets. American officials condemned the Iranian strikes as aggressive acts against countries not directly involved in the conflict. The Pentagon characterized the US military action as necessary to protect American interests and regional partners.

The Kuwait airport attack marks a significant expansion of Iranian military operations beyond direct confrontation with US forces. The targeting of civilian infrastructure in a neutral country raises concerns about the widening scope of the conflict. Kuwait serves as a major transportation hub for the Gulf region, and the suspension of flights affects thousands of travelers and regional commerce.

The escalating strikes between the two countries follow weeks of rising tensions in the Middle East. Iran's decision to attack Kuwait and attempt strikes on Bahrain suggests a strategy of pressuring US allies rather than engaging American forces directly. The damage to Kuwait's airport and the wounding of civilians represent a shift in the nature of the conflict, bringing the war's consequences to countries that have sought to remain on the sidelines.

cards.headline: Seven Killed After Drone Hits Bus in Russian-Controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol was struck by a drone in Russian-occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
A drone strike killed seven people on a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Crimea, according to Russian officials. The incident occurred in the Russian-occupied peninsula that Moscow seized from Ukraine in 2014.

Drone attacks have become a regular occurrence throughout the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, contributing to the mounting civilian toll of the war.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 10 Percent Tariffs on 60 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The US government announced plans for new tariffs of at least 10 percent on most trading partners following a forced labor investigation.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs of at least 10 percent on roughly 60 countries, citing findings from an investigation into forced labor trade practices. The levies would affect major trading partners including Canada, Mexico, and the European Union.

The administration justified the tariffs as a response to what it characterized as unreasonable trade practices that restrict US commerce. The move represents a broad expansion of US trade barriers across multiple economic sectors and regions.

cards.headline: UK Investigates Police Who Handcuffed Dying Student Henry Nowak
cards.teaser: British authorities are investigating officers who handcuffed a student while he was dying from a stab wound.
cards.body:
British authorities are investigating officers who restrained Henry Nowak with handcuffs while he suffered from a fatal stab wound. Video evidence shows Nowak saying he could not breathe while in police custody, prompting public outcry and demonstrations in Southampton.

A government minister has condemned the riots that erupted following Nowak's death and called for a review of police anti-racism guidance. The incident has become heavily politicized as the public demands accountability from law enforcement.

cards.headline: Shell Operated Nigeria Pipeline for Years Despite Pollution Evidence
cards.teaser: Documents show the oil company continued pumping oil through a Nigerian pipeline despite evidence of environmental damage.
cards.body:
Documents obtained through investigation show that Shell continued pumping oil through a Nigerian pipeline for years after receiving evidence of pollution from the infrastructure. The operation persisted despite the documented environmental damage.

Shell stated that the documents lack critical context about the complex operating environment in Nigeria at that time. The company has faced ongoing scrutiny regarding its environmental practices in the Niger Delta region, where oil extraction has caused significant pollution affecting local communities.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Canadian officials formally asked the US and Mexico to renew the USMCA free trade agreement.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal through a letter from Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc to his North American counterparts. The agreement, which replaced NAFTA, governs commerce between Canada, the United States, and Mexico.

The renewal proposal comes amid growing trade tensions, as the Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on Canada and other trading partners. The USMCA is subject to periodic review under its terms.

cards.headline: Missing New Jersey Congressman Tom Kean Jr. Wins Primary After Trump Endorsement
cards.teaser: Republican lawmaker Tom Kean Jr. secured his party's nomination despite not being seen in Washington or his district for months.
cards.body:
Republican Representative Tom Kean Jr. won his primary election in New Jersey's seventh district despite being absent from public view since March. He last cast a House floor vote on March 5 and has not been seen in Washington or his home district since then. Kean was running unopposed in the Republican primary.

Former President Trump endorsed Kean before the primary vote. On the Democratic side, navy helicopter pilot Rebecca Bennett won her party's primary, which featured multiple candidates and significant fundraising. Bennett will face Kean in the general election.

cards.headline: Trump administration scraps $1.8 billion payout fund after Republican opposition
cards.teaser: The Justice Department will not proceed with a fund proposed by the Trump administration after GOP lawmakers objected.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department will not proceed with a $1.8 billion fund that Trump had proposed. The decision came after significant pushback from Republican lawmakers in Congress.

The fund, described by some as an anti-weaponization initiative, faced scrutiny both in Congress and in the courts. The opposition from GOP members proved decisive in forcing the administration to reverse course on the initiative.

cards.headline: California governor race remains tight as Hilton and Becerra lead early returns
cards.teaser: Early results show two candidates ahead in California's all-party primary for governor, with vote counting continuing.
cards.body:
California's primary election on Tuesday will narrow the governor's race to two finalists who advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation. Hilton and Becerra held leads in early returns, though the outcome remained uncertain as officials continued ballot counting.

The state's notoriously slow vote-counting system means results from the tightest races may take days to become clear. Beyond the governor's race, voters also decided high-stakes contests for Los Angeles mayor and multiple congressional seats.

cards.headline: Six states hold midterm primary elections, shaping November ballot
cards.teaser: California, Iowa, and four other states selected candidates in primary elections that will determine matchups for control of Congress.
cards.body:
Six states held primary elections to select candidates for November's midterm contests. California and Iowa voters joined four other states in choosing nominees for congressional and state races.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to a runoff election in California. In Iowa, Democrat Josh Turek secured a nomination to face Trump-backed Ashley Hinson in a bid to flip the red Senate seat.

cards.headline: State Senator Scott Wiener advances in race to succeed Nancy Pelosi
cards.teaser: Scott Wiener will move to the general election in the contest to represent Pelosi's former San Francisco congressional district.
cards.body:
State Senator Scott Wiener advanced to the general election in the race to succeed Nancy Pelosi in Congress. Multiple news outlets projected him as one of the top two finishers in the primary election.

Connie Chan competed closely for the second general election spot. The House seat became available following Pelosi's departure from the House of Representatives.

cards.headline: Trump-backed Representative Randy Feenstra loses Iowa governor primary
cards.teaser: Representative Randy Feenstra, who had Trump's endorsement, was defeated in Iowa's Republican primary for governor.
cards.body:
Representative Randy Feenstra lost the Iowa Republican primary for governor despite backing from former President Trump. Politico reported the defeat as a setback for Trump's influence in the state's gubernatorial contest.

Feenstra currently represents Iowa in the U.S. House of Representatives. His loss in the primary means another candidate will carry the Republican nomination into the general election for governor.

cards.headline: Drone strike kills seven on bus in Russian-controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in occupied Crimea was hit by a drone, killing seven people.
cards.body:
A drone attack on a bus in Russian-controlled Ukraine killed seven people. The bus was traveling between Moscow and Simferopol, the capital of Crimea, which Russia has occupied since 2014.

Ukraine and most international governments consider Crimea to be Ukrainian territory under Russian military occupation.

hero.headline: SpaceX Plans $75 Billion IPO at $135 Per Share
hero.body:
SpaceX is planning a major initial public offering valued at $1.75 trillion, according to details revealed in a flotation prospectus. The aerospace company, led by Elon Musk, aims to raise capital for its ambitious plans to make life "multiplanetary" while expanding its existing business operations.

The company encompasses multiple business segments: the core rocket launch business serving clients like NASA, the Starlink satellite broadband service, the xAI artificial intelligence startup, and the social media platform X, formerly Twitter. Each segment shows different financial performance and growth trajectories.

SpaceX reported a net loss of $4.9 billion on revenues of $18.7 billion in 2025, though revenue grew by a third compared to 2024. Losses have actually widened since the start of the year, with the company losing $4.3 billion in the first quarter alone compared to $528 million in the same period last year. Capital expenditure reached $20.7 billion, with the xAI unit accounting for $12.7 billion, primarily for building large datacentres.

Breaking down the segments, connectivity generated the most revenue at $11.4 billion, followed by the space business at $4.1 billion and AI at $3.2 billion. Starlink was the only profitable segment in the first quarter of this year, while the AI unit lost $6.4 billion in 2025 due to computing expenses for developing and operating AI models.

The prospectus includes ambitious future plans extending beyond typical business projections. SpaceX envisions markets in space tourism, energy production and manufacturing on the moon and Mars, and asteroid mining. The company acknowledges these markets "do not exist today" but expects them to develop over time. More near-term ambitions include launching datacentres in space powered by solar energy, with plans to launch these as soon as 2028.

Musk will retain substantial control of the business following the IPO, maintaining voting power of just over 85 percent through majority ownership of class B shares, which carry ten votes per share compared to class A shares held by other investors. This structure makes it extremely difficult to remove him from leadership.

The IPO positions Musk to accumulate additional wealth, though the exact amount depends on specific conditions. He has been granted one billion class B shares that vest only if SpaceX establishes a permanent human colony on Mars with at least one million inhabitants and achieves market cap targets reaching $7.5 trillion. He also received another 302 million class B shares granted in March that vest upon completing space-based datacentres delivering 100 terawatts of compute annually.

Despite his vast wealth and these potential earnings, Musk maintains a base salary of $54,000 annually, unchanged since 2019.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise as Middle East Fighting Continues
cards.teaser: Oil prices jumped as hostilities continued between the United States and Iran, with peace negotiations at a standstill.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed amid escalating military tensions in the Middle East. Market concerns about potential disruptions to regional oil supplies drove the increases, as traders closely monitored the conflict's impact on production and shipping routes.

The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned that consequences from the Middle East conflict are likely to persist. Energy markets have remained volatile as geopolitical risks continue to shape commodity prices and broader economic outlooks.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over Wind Farm Deal
cards.teaser: Seven states filed suit against the Trump administration over a nearly $1 billion payment to halt an offshore wind farm project.
cards.body:
Seven states sued the Trump administration over a deal that paid French company TotalEnergies nearly $1 billion to stop building an offshore wind farm. New York was among the states challenging the agreement, which they argue improperly uses federal funds to block renewable energy development.

The lawsuit comes as the administration faces criticism from coastal states that support offshore wind development. The states argue the deal undermines their clean energy goals and sets a precedent for using federal payments to prevent renewable energy projects.

cards.headline: Global Economy Expected to Slow Despite Potential Oil Price Peak
cards.teaser: The OECD said Middle East conflicts will continue to affect the global economy even if oil prices stabilize soon.
cards.body:
The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned that global economic growth will slow this year, with the Middle East war's effects expected to persist beyond any near-term peak in oil prices. The organization projects that geopolitical instability will continue to weigh on worldwide economic activity.

The conflict's ripple effects extend across multiple sectors. Policymakers and businesses are assessing how regional instability disrupts trade, energy markets, and consumer confidence globally, with some economies particularly vulnerable to prolonged economic strain.

cards.headline: Stock Market Reaches New Records on AI Stock Gains
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 closed at another record high as artificial intelligence stocks continued their rally.
cards.body:
Stock futures showed little change after the S&P 500 closed at a fresh record, extending gains driven by artificial intelligence companies. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also reached a new high, with both indices posting their longest winning streaks of the year.

AI-related stocks carried the market rally, with companies like Arm, IBM, and HPE posting significant gains. The strength in technology stocks helped Wall Street overcome concerns about Middle East conflicts and inflation, as investors focused on growth potential in artificial intelligence applications.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires 60 Minutes Anchor Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: CBS dismissed Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes after months of tensions between staff and the network's editor in chief.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent, following months of internal conflict at the network. The dismissal came as part of a broader overhaul that also resulted in the termination of the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

During a staff meeting, Pelley directly criticized CBS News management and editor-in-chief Bari Weiss over the firings. The shake-up reflects escalating tensions between staff members and Weiss, whose appointment as editor in chief marked a significant shift in the network's editorial direction.

cards.headline: UK Publishers Can Opt Out of Google AI Search Results
cards.teaser: Britain's competition regulator said publishers will be able to exclude their content from Google's AI-generated search results.
cards.body:
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has announced new conduct requirements that will give publishers the ability to opt out of having their content used in Google's AI search features, including AI Overviews. Publishers will now have tools to prevent their material from being scraped to train Google's AI models and power AI-generated search summaries.

The regulator said this change strengthens publishers' negotiating position when discussing content licensing deals with Google. The decision responds to longstanding concerns from news organizations about how their work is used by AI systems without compensation or control.

hero.headline: Microsoft testing wearable AI device for office workers
hero.body:
Microsoft is testing a wearable AI device designed for office workers, the company revealed during its Build 2026 developer conference. The device represents the company's latest effort to integrate artificial intelligence into workplace tools and hardware.

The announcement came alongside several software developments, including new Work IQ APIs that aim to help developers build AI-powered workplace applications. Microsoft also introduced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed specifically for AI agents rather than traditional apps. This shift reflects the company's vision of software that can act autonomously on behalf of users rather than requiring direct interaction.

Microsoft unveiled new AI models intended to reduce its reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers building AI-powered applications. The move comes as the company seeks to balance its high-profile partnership with OpenAI against the need to control its own AI infrastructure and reduce expenses associated with third-party models.

The Build conference focused on positioning Windows as a trusted platform for development. Microsoft emphasized tools and features aimed at developers, including new Linux tools and an RTX Spark desktop environment for Windows developers. These announcements reflect the company's ongoing effort to attract developers across different platforms and ecosystems.

The wearable AI device remains in testing, and Microsoft has not announced a release timeline or detailed specifications. The company's experimentation with wearable technology follows broader industry trends toward integrating AI into everyday devices beyond smartphones and computers. Other major technology companies have also explored AI-powered wearables, though few have achieved widespread adoption in workplace settings.

cards.headline: Cyera nears $300 million funding round at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The cybersecurity company is seeking funding at 80 times its annual recurring revenue despite operating losses.
cards.body:
Cyera is approaching a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners, which would value the cybersecurity company at $12 billion. This represents an 80 times multiple on the company's annual recurring revenue.

The company specializes in data security and protection. Cyera is currently operating at a loss.

cards.headline: Uber robotaxis accumulate lost items including dentures and Squishmallows
cards.teaser: The ride-hailing company has found thousands of items left behind in autonomous vehicles.
cards.body:
Uber has recovered thousands of items left behind in its robotaxis, ranging from Squishmallows stuffed animals to dentures and a bag reading "I Heart Hot Dads." The lost items highlight an ongoing challenge in the autonomous vehicle industry.

Even in a future of robot taxis, someone still has to return the things passengers leave behind. The company must maintain systems for cataloging, storing, and returning lost property to riders, a task that remains labor-intensive despite the automation of driving itself.

cards.headline: God of War spinoff to follow character Laufey on PlayStation 5
cards.teaser: Santa Monica Studio announced the game will center on Kratos' wife Faye.
cards.body:
Sony announced God of War Laufey, a spinoff developed by Santa Monica Studio and coming to PlayStation 5. The game was revealed during Sony's State of Play presentation, though a release date hasn't been set yet.

The spinoff expands the God of War franchise beyond its main character, offering players a new direction within the series.

cards.headline: Male bowerbirds using bright human-made items to attract mates
cards.teaser: Researchers observed the birds incorporating manufactured objects into courtship displays.
cards.body:
Male bowerbirds are using bright human-made items in their elaborate courtship displays to attract females. The behavior demonstrates how the birds are adapting their mating rituals to include manufactured objects alongside natural materials.

Researchers described the phenomenon as a reminder of how human activity is changing the natural world in unanticipated ways. Bowerbirds are known for building intricate structures and decorating them with colorful objects to impress potential mates, and the incorporation of human-made items represents an evolution of this longstanding behavior.

cards.headline: Ubisoft remaking Rayman Legends as 3D game for October release
cards.teaser: Rayman Legends Retold will launch October 1 across multiple platforms including Nintendo Switch 2.
cards.body:
Ubisoft is bringing Rayman Legends to three dimensions with Rayman Legends Retold, launching October 1 across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and other platforms. All versions will feature identical content.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version will run at 60 frames per second. Ubisoft gave journalists hands-on time with the remake, allowing them to play for approximately two hours.

cards.headline: Stuntman game series returns with Hollywood film tie-ins
cards.teaser: Sony announced Stuntman Hollywood for PlayStation 5 featuring vehicles from Universal films.
cards.body:
Sony revealed Stuntman Hollywood during its State of Play presentation, reviving the driving game series with tie-ins to Universal films. The game will feature vehicles and stunts from major movie franchises including Fast and Furious and Back to the Future.

The game is coming soon to PlayStation 5. The Stuntman series previously focused on movie-inspired driving and stunt challenges. The new entry brings licensed vehicles from recognizable film properties to the gameplay.

hero.headline: Knicks and Spurs open NBA Finals in San Antonio
hero.teaser: The NBA Finals tip off with Game 1 between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs.
hero.body:
The New York Knicks will face the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC in San Antonio. The Spurs earned their spot in the championship series by defeating the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory, finishing with 22 points and seven rebounds. The 22-year-old French star was named series MVP and became emotional after clinching the Finals berth. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said when explaining his reaction. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, Wembanyama's performance was supported by strong contributions from his teammates. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points, including six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper provided scoring off the bench. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, made a crucial block in the fourth quarter as the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt. After the game, Wembanyama credited his teammates' effort, saying "They don't know how much I love them, and everyone stepped up tonight."

The Thunder fought hard despite playing without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, scored 35 points and distributed nine assists but couldn't prevent his team from relinquishing their title. No other Thunder player scored more than 20 points.

Coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the tough loss but expressed confidence in his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The Spurs head into the Finals with historical momentum on their side. The last time the Knicks appeared in the NBA Finals was 1999, when they faced the Spurs and lost the series 4-1. The Knicks are attempting to win their first championship since 1973.

Julian Champagnie reflected on the Spurs' achievement after the game, noting the importance of having elite talent. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said.

League executives have weighed in on five key questions heading into the matchup. Experts have also made their predictions for which franchise will claim the Larry O'Brien Trophy and who will earn Finals MVP honors. The series features two storied franchises competing for the championship, with the Spurs holding home court advantage for the opening game.

cards.headline: Golden Knights rally past Hurricanes in Stanley Cup Final opener
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights overcame an early deficit to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final on Tuesday night at Lenovo Center.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final on Tuesday night in Raleigh. Tomas Hertl broke a third-period deadlock with the winning goal at 16:36, marking his fourth postseason goal. Shea Theodore contributed three points for Vegas, while Brett Howden, Ivan Barbashev, and William Karlsson also scored.

Carolina squandered an early two-goal lead as the Golden Knights mounted their comeback. The victory gives Vegas an early advantage in the series and moves them three wins closer to a second Stanley Cup championship.

cards.headline: Charles Leclerc signs new long-term contract with Ferrari
cards.teaser: The Ferrari driver has committed his future to the team ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc has signed a new long-term contract with Ferrari, the team confirmed ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix. The agreement keeps the driver with the Italian team as they continue their competitive campaign in Formula One.

The timing of the contract extension is notable, coming just before Leclerc's home race at Monaco, one of the most prestigious events on the racing calendar.

cards.headline: Aston Villa forward Kirsty Hanson to join Tottenham
cards.teaser: The Women's Super League top scorer is set to move to Spurs after an impressive season.
cards.body:
Aston Villa forward Kirsty Hanson is set to join Tottenham after an impressive season in the Women's Super League, where she was the club's top scorer.

The transfer strengthens Tottenham's attacking options as they prepare for the upcoming campaign.

cards.headline: FIFA president Gianni Infantino marks decade in office
cards.teaser: Ten years after succeeding Sepp Blatter, Infantino's tenure draws mixed assessments from those around the game.
cards.body:
Gianni Infantino has completed ten years leading FIFA, having assumed the role after Sepp Blatter's departure. His legacy remains contested among those closely connected to international football.

Assessments of his presidency defy simple categorization. Whether viewed as a reformer or ringleader within the organization, experts suggest his decade-long tenure warrants more nuanced evaluation than straightforward labeling allows.

cards.headline: Formula One evaluates 2026 rules ahead of Monaco Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Analysis examines whether new regulations will enable overtaking at the circuit where it is most difficult.
cards.body:
The 2026 Formula One regulations have raised questions about their impact on racing at Monaco, where overtaking opportunities are traditionally scarce. The new rules introduce what observers call "yo-yo racing," a term used to describe the anticipated competitive dynamics under the changes.

BBC Sport's Andrew Benson examines whether these 2026 regulations will alter the character of the Monaco Grand Prix and improve passing opportunities at the historic street circuit where racing has historically been constrained by limited overtaking possibilities.

cards.headline: Updated prospect rankings released for all 30 MLB teams
cards.teaser: New evaluations identify rising and falling players across major league farm systems entering June.
cards.body:
Updated top 10 prospect rankings for all 30 Major League Baseball teams have been released as the calendar turns to June. The rankings identify which players are rising and falling within their respective farm systems.

The evaluations provide a snapshot of organizational depth across baseball as teams approach the midpoint of the minor league season. The updated rankings reflect recent performance and development trajectories for prospects throughout the sport.

hero.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley From 60 Minutes
hero.body:
CBS News terminated Scott Pelley from his position at 60 Minutes following a heated confrontation with network leadership over recent staff cuts and editorial direction, according to reporting from the Guardian and other outlets.

Pelley, who joined 60 Minutes in 2004, was fired after clashing with executives during a Monday morning staff meeting. The termination came days after CBS News management dismissed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents: Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi. No specific reasons were given for those initial terminations.

During the Monday meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton, Pelley directly criticized Bari Weiss, CBS News's editor-in-chief who joined the network in October. "She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said, according to the Guardian. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

After the meeting, Weiss and other executives met with Pelley on Tuesday and told him his behavior was inappropriate. That same evening, Bilton sent Pelley a termination message stating he was fired "for cause effective immediately." In the message, Bilton cited Pelley's conduct during the staff meeting, writing: "Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Bilton also notified the staff of Pelley's departure, telling them he had made repeated attempts to communicate with Pelley over the weekend and tried to find common ground that afternoon. "That was not the path Scott chose," he wrote in a message obtained by the Guardian.

The firings mark significant changes at 60 Minutes following the Skydance acquisition of CBS parent company Paramount. Pelley had previously announced his satisfaction with the new management in December, stating the show was conducting stories with the same rigor and experiencing no corporate interference. However, nine days later, Alfonsi informed colleagues that Weiss had blocked her story about a prison in El Salvador for what Alfonsi described as "political" reasons, sparking major controversy at the network.

Pelley's departure further depletes 60 Minutes' correspondent roster. With journalist Anderson Cooper leaving earlier this year and now Pelley's termination, the show retains only three full-time correspondents: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and L Jon Wertheim. CBS News journalist and former evening news anchor Norah O'Donnell contributes to the show.

Pelley first joined CBS News in 1989 and served as chief White House correspondent and anchor of the CBS Evening News from 2011 to 2017. Rome Hartman, a longtime 60 Minutes producer, called Pelley "among the all-time greats of CBS News and of 60 Minutes" and criticized the network's decision to terminate him for pushing back aggressively during a staff meeting.

cards.headline: Karen Bass Advances to November Runoff for Los Angeles Mayor
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass secured a spot in the November runoff election.
cards.body:
Incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to the November runoff election after winning the primary with less than 50% of the vote. Bass finished in first place in Tuesday's primary results.

Bass will face either Republican newcomer and reality TV star Spencer Pratt or fellow Democrat city council member Nithya Raman in November. As of Tuesday evening, the second-place finisher had not yet been officially determined between Pratt and Raman.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton Lead California Governor Primary
cards.teaser: Two candidates are leading early returns in the California gubernatorial primary race.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton emerged at the top of California's crowded gubernatorial primary in early returns, with Democrat Tom Steyer trailing in third place. The race remained too close to call, with many ballots still uncounted. Two Democratic candidates—San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa—conceded shortly after polls closed.

California's primary system advances the top two vote-getters to the November general election regardless of party affiliation. Given the state's notoriously slow vote-counting process, final results for the tightest races may take several days to be officially determined.

cards.headline: India Clears Release of Oscar-Nominated Film After Initial Ban
cards.teaser: The Voice of Hind Rajab has been approved for release after censorship controversy.
cards.body:
India's Central Board of Film Certification cleared Kaouther Ben Hania's Oscar-nominated feature The Voice of Hind Rajab for release after initially blocking the film in March. The board had previously censored the film over concerns about its political sensitivity and potential impact on India-Israel relations.

The film tells the story of Hind Rajab. After weeks of controversy in India over the initial censorship decision, the board reversed its position and approved the theatrical release of the feature.

cards.headline: UK Publishers Can Opt Out of Google AI Search Results
cards.teaser: Competition regulator says new policy strengthens publisher negotiating position.
cards.body:
Publishers in the United Kingdom can now opt out of having their content used in Google's AI search features. The Competition and Markets Authority announced the policy change, giving publishers control over whether their material powers AI-driven search summaries and related features.

The watchdog's decision strengthens publishers' negotiating position with Google regarding content deals. By providing publishers with tools to prevent their content from training AI models, the regulator addresses concerns about tech companies using published material without compensation or publisher consent.

cards.headline: Michael Stipe and Andrew Watt Perform New Song on Kimmel
cards.teaser: The musicians showcased their collaborative track from a recent HBO series.
cards.body:
Michael Stipe and Andrew Watt performed their collaborative song I Played the Fool on a late-night talk show. The track appeared during the opening credits of Steve Carell's recent HBO series Rooster.

The performance gave audiences a chance to see the two musicians present the song in a live setting. The collaboration between Stipe, former frontman of R.E.M., and producer-musician Watt marks their work together on the HBO series soundtrack.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Praises Paul McCartney's New Album
cards.teaser: The singer expressed admiration for the former Beatle's latest release.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift showed appreciation for Paul McCartney's new album, writing that she is never not inspired by his work. McCartney released his first album in five years, The Boys of Dungeon Lane, in May.

Swift's public praise highlights the cross-generational influence of the former Beatle. McCartney's latest album marks his return to recording after a five-year gap between studio releases.

hero.headline: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton lead in California governor primary
hero.teaser: Democrats Xavier Becerra, Katie Porter, and Tom Steyer competed against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
hero.body:
California's gubernatorial primary election remained too close to call Tuesday night, with early results showing a tight three-way contest at the top of the race. With many ballots still uncounted, the Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer emerged as the leading candidates.

Two Democratic candidates conceded shortly after polls closed. San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa both withdrew from contention as results came in. However, the final standings could shift significantly in the coming days, as California's mail-in voting system and careful ballot verification process means counting could take weeks.

Becerra and Hilton expressed confidence about advancing to the general election. Steyer told supporters in San Francisco that he remained a contender, noting that all ballots needed to be counted before determining the race's direction.

California's gubernatorial primary featured an unusually crowded field of 61 candidates, making it one of the most chaotic elections in recent state history. The race to succeed term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom lacked a clear frontrunner after several prominent Democrats declined to run, including Senator Alex Padilla and Attorney General Rob Bonta.

The state's "jungle" primary system, which advances only the top two vote-getters regardless of party affiliation, created concerns among Democrats. Some worried that a fragmented Democratic field could inadvertently allow two Republicans to advance, potentially resulting in the state's first Republican governor since Arnold Schwarzenegger's reelection in 2006.

Voters expressed frustration about housing affordability, homelessness, wildfire risk and rising cost of living. These issues defined much of the campaign as candidates presented competing visions for governing a state whose economy ranks among the world's largest.

Becerra's path to the top was unexpected. The former Biden administration health secretary and California attorney general had languished near the bottom of early polls and faced pressure to drop out. Instead, he mounted a late campaign surge, positioning himself as an experienced public servant capable of navigating economic and political uncertainty. His campaign highlighted his government expertise through a "hot competence summer" effort, though his leadership at HHS faced scrutiny from rivals and former Biden officials.

Steyer, a billionaire investor and climate activist, offered a contrasting progressive approach. He spent over 200 million dollars of his own fortune on the race, presenting himself as an outsider capable of disrupting Sacramento's political establishment. His campaign centered on the unusual proposition that billionaires and corporations should pay higher taxes.

The Democratic Party convention had ended without endorsing any candidate, as no one cleared the required 60 percent threshold. Party leadership largely remained on the sidelines, while labor unions and environmental groups split their support among multiple candidates.

In the Los Angeles mayoral race, incumbent Karen Bass advanced to the general election, with reality TV personality Spencer Pratt leading to capture the second spot against Democrat Nithya Raman.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary in the race to succeed Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham in New Mexico, according to Decision Desk HQ. Haaland celebrated Tuesday night at a historic plaza in Albuquerque's Old Town neighborhood.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first Native American woman elected governor in the United States. She previously served in the Biden administration as Interior Secretary before returning to New Mexico to pursue the gubernatorial seat. Haaland will now advance to the general election as the Democratic nominee.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes as peace talks stall
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged strikes Tuesday as diplomatic efforts stalled and tensions escalated across the Middle East. Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain that were either shot down or failed to reach their targets. The U.S. military launched strikes on an Iranian facility in response to the Iranian attacks.

The confrontation spread beyond direct U.S.-Iran exchanges. Iranian drones struck Kuwait's international airport, causing significant damage and forcing a suspension of traffic. The clashes mark a notable escalation in the long-standing hostility between the two nations as peace negotiations have failed to produce results.

cards.headline: Karen Bass advances to runoff in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass will proceed to the general election, though her opponent has yet to be determined.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to the general election runoff after winning the primary with less than 50% of the vote. She will face one of two candidates in November's general election.

Bass's runoff opponent will be either Republican Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or Democrat Nithya Raman, a city council member. As of Tuesday evening, the race between Pratt and Raman remained too close to call.

cards.headline: Iowa sets general election matchups for governor and Senate
cards.teaser: Republican Zach Lahn and Democrat Rob Sand will compete for governor, while Democrat Josh Turek faces Republican Ashley Hinson for Senate.
cards.body:
Iowa voters have selected their nominees for competitive statewide races this November. Democrat Rob Sand, the state auditor, will face Republican businessman Zach Lahn in the gubernatorial contest. Sand ran unopposed in the Democratic primary, while Lahn won a crowded Republican primary that included U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra.

In the Senate race, Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek will challenge Republican U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson. Democrats see opportunities to compete across multiple statewide and congressional races in the traditionally Republican-leaning state.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley fired from '60 Minutes' after confrontation with new producer
cards.teaser: The veteran anchor was terminated after criticizing new executive producer Nick Bilton and his boss Bari Weiss during a staff meeting.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at '60 Minutes,' was fired following a heated staff meeting where he criticized CBS News management. During the meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley attacked the network's recent decisions to remove the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Pelley's outburst targeted Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief, as part of a broader management overhaul at the long-running program. The confrontation occurred during Bilton's first day leading the show, highlighting tensions among top talent over the leadership changes at '60 Minutes.'

cards.headline: Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Christina Bohannan set for House rematch in Iowa
cards.teaser: The two candidates will face
